title.narrative: To strengthen the defense and protection of Human Rights Defenders (HRDs) in the Philippines, especially women HRDs, and to contribute to efforts to mitigate the risks in their work amidst a worsening climate of impunity.

description.narrative: Incidence of human rights violations (HRVs) human rights defenders (HRDs) in the Philippines (PH) particularly in the most vulnerable sectors of society such as women, youth, children, elderly from indigenous people, peasants, workers, urban poor, environmental defenders and other HR advocates have been reduced as indicated by:

title.narrative: Indicator 1: Substantial reduction in cases of politically and drug related, extrajudicial killings and other incidents of human rights violations such as illegal arrests & trumpedup charges.

description.narrative: Indicator 1: Substantial reduction in cases of politically and drug related, extrajudicial killings and other incidents of human rights violations such as illegal arrests & trumpedup charges.

comment.narrative: From July 2016 to March 2021 Karapatan documented 394 victims of EJKs perpetrated in line with the counterinsurgency program with 207 rights defenders killed. Karapatan documentation also shows at least 493 victims of frustrated killings these victims have survived or have escaped from attempts by suspected perpetrators from State actors 1090 victims of illegal arrest and detention based on trumped up charges. Reports of numbers of alleged drug suspects that have been killed during police operations vary from 8000 to around 30000 since President Duterte took office in 2016.

description.narrative: The project partners conducted at least 1 physical engagement of 2 individuals at UNHRC and submitted at least 2 reports for the 2017 UPR. NCCP, NUPL and EcuVoice from 2019 to 2021 conducted at least 2 physical engagements of 11 individuals at the UNHRC. Lobbied to 25 Missions and delivered 5 live oral interventions at the UNHRC (42nd and 43rd sessions). Delivered 10 recorded oral interventions during UNHRC Sessions. Reports were also submitted to OHCHR in 2019 during the 44th UN Human Rights Council, and was later compiled to a compendium that was distributed to international partners and embassies in Manila and in Geneva.

comment.narrative: NCCP NUPL and EcuVoice from 2019 to 2021 conducted at least 2 physical engagements of 11 individuals at the UNHRC. Reports were also submitted to OHCHR in 2019 during the 44th UN Human Rights Council and was later compiled to a compendium that was distributed to international partners and embassies in Manila and in Geneva.
At least 15 international organisations UNHRC and EUMS institutions reached by factbased lobbying physical and online meeting.
